notes:
[Jonathan Bentley] Trust is a security concept. Usually these errors indicate a FW (uCode) bug or a security exploitation. I think "Trust" is associated with "Sunpass" and can be reported either inside the Core or in the Ubox.
Trust can be associated with branching or registers. Essentially, we make certain uCode flows "Trusted" (or Trusted Paths) and you are not allowed to branch into the middle of those flows without continuing that trust. This is an effort to prevent someone from jumping into the middle of those flows that should not be. We can also have registers that are Trusted and can only be accessed from within those flows, I believe.
I will defer to the Security experts for more details descriptions, but that is the high level picture of the feature.
So, usually a uCode bug or an attempted security exploration is the reason for these types of failure. Almost always a uCode bug though, if I recall correctly. This can be fixed via patch and should not require any type of part replacement.

notes:
[Jonathan Bentley] Trust is a security concept. Usually these errors indicate a FW (uCode) bug or a security exploitation. I think "Trust" is associated with "Sunpass" and can be reported either inside the Core or in the Ubox.
Trust can be associated with branching or registers. Essentially, we make certain uCode flows "Trusted" (or Trusted Paths) and you are not allowed to branch into the middle of those flows without continuing that trust. This is an effort to prevent someone from jumping into the middle of those flows that should not be. We can also have registers that are Trusted and can only be accessed from within those flows, I believe.
I will defer to the Security experts for more details descriptions, but that is the high level picture of the feature.
So, usually a uCode bug or an attempted security exploration is the reason for these types of failure. Almost always a uCode bug though, if I recall correctly. This can be fixed via patch and should not require any type of part replacement.

description: Poisoned Read Data when Poison Disabled
action: [Unexpected Poison Consumption] Verify system have latest microcode. CPU is in non poison mode and poison is detected. This failure is detected by CPU and it likely originated by a Memory or IO subsystem. Debug Poison Src; Possible Memory /PCIe. Check the address in UCNA depository list. If no match and none of the IMC mcbanks had overflown then the processor may have been the source of the poison. Contact your Intel representative to assist debugging poison error source.
notes: [Ling, Jing] Poison can be set by either poison indication from CMI (which means core or CHA is setting poison) or by MC detecting an uncorrectable ECC error. Normally, we would expect any such condition to result in the fatal error in source and bring down the system. Then MC won’t see this 0x00B0 condition. But if for some reason the system wasn’t brought down (or in time), you will get this error. This is like any uncorrectable data error condition (e.g., uncorrectable ECC error) when poison is disabled or any fatal error condition. The action should be bringing down the system. The error is not necessarily in DIMM as poison could be coming from core.
